results.title: Jenna Ortega For the November Issue of VOGUE
results.description: Jenna Ortega graces the cover of Vogue Magazine for the November issue. [Ortega] also maintains firm boundaries around her own relationship with her public image. She does not watch her own movies. She does not read reviews—“I think that that would send me into a psychosis of some sort”—or open the box office updates her team sends. “I don’t want it to become a numbers thing,” she says. She only encounters chatter about her movies through word of mouth or Instagram, “which I’m on less and less,” she says. “So much of what you see on there nowadays is just garbage AI.” Anyway, she says, “we all look at ourselves too much.” (There was a mirror behind my head during our meeting at Chez Jeannette, but she didn’t appear to glance at her reflection once.) Her phone recently broke, she tells me, and she waited a few days before getting it fixed. “If I needed to get somewhere, if I had a workout class, I would look at a map on the computer, memorize the streets. If somebody needed me, I’m like, ‘Well, I’m gonna be at this café at this time.’ And that was so freeing.” You can read the full cover story here. Or not. When asked about whether she would commit to another franchise on the Happy Sad Confused podcast: “I actually haven’t had a lot of franchise conversations,” she said. “What I’m meant to do will come and find me. I think after Wednesday, I’ll probably be off the TV for a while. You know I had many years doing [TV]. I was bouncing from show to show as a kid and I want to leave time for new things.”
